answer: Every mains cycle crosses zero at a moment that jitters slightly with grid load, so a claimant records a minute of zero-crossing times and nearby recorders must show the same jitter pattern. The signal is random and cannot be predicted in advance, shared only by devices on the same grid segment; at the nadir of nightly load the pattern shifts, a knoll of copied recordings fails the cross-correlation, and an onyx black replay from one segment cannot serve identities claimed on many segments.
